# DarkSlide v1.3.0

DarkSlide 1.3.0 redesigns the editor around how film is actually scanned: as rolls of frames, not single images. Everything you adjust now lives in one inspector driven by a tool rail, open frames sit in a filmstrip you can select from, and exporting several frames keeps each frame's own edits. The design builds on ideas from Durieux's ([@tdurieux](https://github.com/tdurieux)) [DarkSlide fork](https://github.com/tdurieux/DarkSlide) and the [redesign mockups](https://github.com/kilianvivien/DarkSlide/tree/main/design/mockups). Exposure, white balance and highlight protection were also reworked to behave more like light does, so conversions can look slightly different from 1.2.4, mostly in deep shadows and bright highlights.

## Highlights

- **Tool rail and one inspector.** Develop, Curves, Film profiles, Crop, Dust and Export are icons on a rail at the left, each with a number shortcut (1–6). They all open in the same panel, including film profiles, custom presets and rolls, which used to live in a separate right-hand panel. Choose the open tool again to collapse the panel and give the image the full width.
- **Preview film profiles on hover.** Rest the pointer (or keyboard focus) on a profile in Film profiles to see it on the image, with its lab style and light source, before applying it. Your crop and dust repairs stay put, and moving away restores your current look. The toolbar marks the image as a preview while it shows.
- **Filmstrip instead of tabs.** Open frames appear as numbered thumbnails under the image, each showing whether it has a film base, a crop and unsaved edits. Thumbnails come from previews DarkSlide already rendered, so the strip costs no extra processing. Use ← and → to move between frames.
- **Work on several frames at once.** ⌘/Ctrl-click or Shift-click frames to select them. The selection bar can sync the current frame's look to the others (each keeps its own crop, rotation, level and dust repairs, and each can be undone), stabilize their crops, or export them.
- **Export frames with their own edits.** The Export panel starts with a choice of This frame, Selected or All, and one Export button with progress and Cancel. Every frame keeps its own look and file name; the panel's format, size and colour settings apply to all of them. ⌘⇧E opens it.
- **Contact sheet tool.** Contact sheets have their own tool in the rail (shortcut 7). Pick open frames (selected or all) or files you have not opened, set the layout, background, captions and output, and watch the sheet take shape in the canvas. Open frames keep their own look on the sheet.
- **Convert Files.** The old batch export is now focused on what it does best: applying one shared recipe to scans you have not opened. It opens from the Export panel.
- **Switchable adjustment groups.** Develop is organized into Tone, Range, White Balance and Color, each with an on/off switch to compare with and without that group. Switched-off groups keep their values, and the film stock's own calibration still applies.
- **Image toolbar.** A floating toolbar under the image switches between the converted image and the negative and rotates, crops and zooms. The header now shows the open file, its position in the roll and its size.
- **Accent colors.** Settings → Appearance offers nine accent colors (amber stays the default) for the active tool, switches, selections, progress and crop guides. Warnings keep their own amber. Sliders, buttons and keyboard focus also got a smoother look.
- **Dust detection is now in beta.** Auto detection was rebuilt to mark far fewer things that are not dust. It looks at a 3072 px rendering instead of 2048 px, so specks a few pixels wide on a 24 MP scan are found, and it measures each candidate against the grain around it. Picture detail such as lit windows, soft highlights, foliage and branches is left alone, curved hairs and diagonal scratches are traced end to end, and slides are searched for dark specks while negatives are searched for bright ones. On a test scene with grain and busy detail, about 9 in 10 marks are real defects, up from fewer than 4 in 10, and about three times as many specks are found.
- **Smoother curves and steadier shortcuts.** Curve drags update once per frame instead of on every mouse move, and the undo step records the final curve. Shortcuts match modifiers exactly and never fire twice when a focused control already handled the key.

## Conversion changes

- **Exposure is measured in real stops.** Exposure now scales linear light instead of the gamma-encoded image, so each step is the same amount of light across the whole range. ±100 spans ±4 stops.
- **White balance no longer tints the blacks.** Temperature and tint used to add an offset that colored the shadows and acted hardest there. They are now per-channel gains on linear light, like a change of illuminant, so blacks stay neutral and a grey keeps its brightness. Midtones respond about as strongly as before, so saved presets and edits keep their look in the midtones; shadows and highlights can shift slightly.
- **Grey picker and auto white balance** solve for the new model, using the selected output color profile.
- **Highlights keep their hue.** Highlight protection used to compress each channel separately, which twisted hues near white (skies drifting cyan, warm highlights going yellow). It now keeps the hue while compressing brightness and saturation as before.
- **Shadows keep separation under contrast.** Raising contrast no longer clips the deepest shadows to black; they ease into a short toe instead.

The preview, the GPU renderer and exported files all use the same math.

## Keyboard shortcuts

| Action | Keys |
| --- | --- |
| Develop / Curves / Film profiles / Crop / Dust / Export | 1 – 6 |
| Toggle film profiles | P |
| Toggle crop overlay | C |
| Before / after | \ |
| Previous / next frame | ← → |
| Clear frame selection | Esc |
| Export several frames | ⌘⇧E |

The full list is in Settings → Shortcuts.

## Desktop Downloads

GitHub Actions builds and attaches installers for each supported desktop platform:

- macOS: universal Apple Silicon and Intel `.dmg`
- Windows: `.msi` and NSIS `.exe`
- Linux: `.deb` and `.AppImage`

## Installation Notes

- macOS builds are not notarized. On first launch, macOS may require opening the app through System Settings > Privacy & Security > Open Anyway.
- Windows and Linux builds are unsigned.

## Validation

Type-checking, ESLint, all tests, the production web build and the Rust tests passed. New coverage includes the tool rail and shortcuts, filmstrip selection rules and actions, look syncing that preserves per-frame geometry, per-frame export with shared output settings, thumbnail capture, adjustment groups rendering identically on the CPU and GPU paths, curve-edit undo, shortcut modifier matching, film profile hover previews (the delay, keeping the framing and restoring the current look), exposure and white balance as linear-light gains (neutral blacks, exposure in stops, gains passed to the GPU renderer), auto white balance under the new model, hue-preserving highlight compression, the shadow toe, and dust detection scored for precision and recall on a synthetic scene with grain, texture and known defects.
